::: {.why}
Three algorithms that cover most institutional execution, each optimal against a different benchmark, and the choice of benchmark is a choice about who is being blamed for the outcome.
:::

## What you should be able to do tonight

- Say what benchmark each algorithm minimises deviation from, and when each is the right one.
- Implement all three and compare their realised cost on your own data.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>60 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [35 min]{.task-min} Implement the three in qlib/exec/: TWAP on a clock, VWAP on a forecast volume profile, and a participation-rate algorithm that trades a fixed fraction of observed volume. The middle one needs an intraday volume forecast, which you can build as a simple average profile by time of day from your ITCH sample.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [25 min]{.task-min} Compare them on the same orders: simulate each against your reconstructed book for a set of order sizes, and report realised cost against arrival price and against the day's VWAP. An algorithm that beats VWAP and loses against arrival is doing exactly what it was designed to do, and that is the point of the comparison.
:::
:::

## Deliverable

::: {.deliverable}
Three execution algorithms in qlib/exec/ compared on realised cost against two benchmarks.
:::

## Checkpoint

::: {.checkpoint}
Your algorithm beat VWAP and lost against arrival price. Is that good? Say what each benchmark measures.
:::
